call_points.text: Astec FY27 revenue growth now guided at more than 20%, up from around 20% given on the last call.
call_points.versus_prior: raised from around 20% on the last call

call_points.text: Overall capex guided at ₹300-350 Cr, covering the integrated palm complex and the specialty fats refinery; no new investment beyond this.
Specialty fats refinery, the first, starts ramping in September; downstream expected to add close to 200 bps to overall EBITDA when scaled.
Crop Care hit by a June with a 40% rainfall deficit; recovery call deferred to end of September after the cotton herbicide season.
New launches Ashitaka and Takai together contribute close to 18-20% of Q1 Crop Care sales in their first season.
Dairy hit by LPG-linked packaging inflation from the Middle East war and elevated milk procurement; only about 70% of pricing passed on.
Crop Care EBIT margin expected to hold around 26-27% despite the tough year.
Average net working capital improved significantly year-on-year, supporting cash generation and return on capital.
Milk procurement prices expected to stay elevated for the next 2-3 quarters; packaging inflation seen easing by August.
Bangladesh JV ACI Godrej returned to double-digit growth in volumes, revenue and PBT on a broad-based recovery.
FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at early double digits, with mid-teens PBT growth.
Animal Nutrition guided to double-digit volume-led revenue growth; Crop Care to a high double-digit recovery.
Oil palm guided to another year of early double-digit volume growth, with area expansion targeted above FY26's record.
Animal Nutrition Q4 segment margin included about ₹9.5 Cr of pet food manufacturing income booked in other income.
Creamline Dairy Q4 revenue grew about 5% YoY excluding bulk sales; profitability under pressure from elevated milk procurement costs.
Return on capital employed rose from 16% to 20%, attributed to working-capital focus.
IMD and Skymet predict below-normal monsoon; management kept FY27 guidance unchanged, citing geographic skew and a normal June.
Iran war flagged as an overhang on palm oil and crop protection; Nadir Godrej said the net impact on Agrovet overall may not be great.
Strategic review under way for shrimp, seeds and cattle genetics businesses; no timeline given.
Astec board strengthened with Vishal Sharma as Non-Executive Chairperson, Mathew Eipe as Independent Director and Arijit Mukherjee as Executive Director.

operating_notes.text: Oil palm oil extraction ratio was 20.77% in Q4FY26 versus 19.76% a year earlier, on a small seasonal base of about 60,000 tonnes of FFB against 6,37,000 tonnes annually.
Astec sourced around 47% of its total imports from China last year and is a net exporter, giving a natural hedge to currency depreciation.
About 50% of oil palm trees are in the juvenile 0-4 year stage, which management expects to become productive over the next five years.
Oil Palm OER improved to 18.8% in Q1FY27 from 18.4% a year ago, with FFB volumes flat.
Animal Nutrition mix: cattle feed 55-56% of the segment, fish feed about 7%, with fish feed volumes growing over 20%.
Crop Care's Ashitaka and Takai together contribute close to 18-20% of Q1 segment sales.

timeline.summary: On its 4 May 2026 Q4FY26 call, Godrej Agrovet guided FY27 to double-digit revenue growth and mid-teens PBT growth, with about ₹400 Cr capex and ₹100-125 Cr of surplus cash.

On its 6 August 2026 Q1FY27 call, Godrej Agrovet reported consolidated sales of ₹2,852 Cr, up 10% YoY, with Animal Nutrition and Oil Palm growing while Crop Care revenue fell 16.2% on a delayed monsoon, and cut its FY27 growth guidance from mid-teens to double-digit.
